extracted.intended_audience: USPTO patent examiners (and patent prosecutors / applicants seeking to understand examiner practice)
extracted.subtask_description: A step-by-step examination procedure for determining whether a patent application complies with the written description, enablement, best mode, definiteness, and dependent-claim requirements of 35 U.S.C. §112. Intended to guide examiners through claim construction, prior-art searching, substantive §112 analyses, and Office action preparation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Determine what applicant has invented and is seeking to patent
rubrics_metrics.description: Review the complete specification, including the detailed description of the invention, any specific embodiments that have been disclosed, and the claims. Determine what, precisely, the applicant has invented and how the claims relate to and define that invention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Review the full specification and claims to identify the invention; examine disclosed embodiments and how claim language maps to the disclosed invention. This is the foundational factual determination to guide subsequent claim construction and §112 analyses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interpret the claims
rubrics_metrics.description: Give the claim its broadest reasonable interpretation consistent with the specification as it would be interpreted by one of ordinary skill in the art. Ascertain the boundaries of the subject matter encompassed by each claim.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow MPEP 2111. Determine whether any claim limitation invokes §112, ¶6; if so, construe that limitation to cover the corresponding structure, material, or acts described in the specification and equivalents that perform the stated function. Also determine the effective filing date of each claim (see MPEP 201.11 & 706.02). See PART 1, section II and III.C of the 2011 Supplementary 112 Guidelines for additional guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conduct a thorough search of the prior art
rubrics_metrics.description: Determine the state of the art and identify prior art references that are material to the patentability of the claimed invention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Perform a comprehensive prior-art search to establish the relevant technological background and references material to novelty, non-obviousness, and other patentability issues that may interact with §112 analyses (e.g., to define ordinary skill in the art or what was known at filing).

rubrics_metrics.name: Written description requirement (35 U.S.C. §112, ¶1)
rubrics_metrics.description: Based on the written description, determine whether one of ordinary skill in the art would recognize that the applicant was in possession of the claimed invention as a whole at the time of filing the application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use PART 2, section I of the 2011 Supplementary 112 Guidelines and MPEP 2163. If the description lacks sufficient detail to support the claim, reject the claim as containing subject matter not described in the specification in such a way as to reasonably convey to one skilled in the relevant art that the inventor(s) had possession at filing. See FP 7.31.01 for procedural guidance on such rejections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Enablement requirement (35 U.S.C. §112, ¶1)
rubrics_metrics.description: Based on the broadest reasonable interpretation of the claim, determine if the disclosure enables one skilled in the art to make and use the full scope of the claimed invention without undue experimentation at the time of filing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow MPEP 2164. If the disclosure is not enabling, reject the claims as containing subject matter not described in the specification in such a way as to enable one skilled in the art to make and/or use the invention (see FP 7.31.02). If lack of enablement is due to the scope of the claims, use FP 7.31.03. Consider scope versus teaching and whether undue experimentation would be required across the claim scope.

rubrics_metrics.name: Best mode requirement (35 U.S.C. §112, ¶1)
rubrics_metrics.description: Confirm whether the best mode of practicing the claimed invention is disclosed in the application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assume that the best mode is disclosed in the specification unless there is evidence showing the inventor possessed a best mode at filing and did not disclose it (see MPEP 2165). For cases with evidence of concealment of the best mode, follow FP 7.31.04. Evaluate whether an inventor's undisclosed preference rises to a best-mode concealment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definiteness requirement (35 U.S.C. §112, ¶2)
rubrics_metrics.description: Under the broadest reasonable interpretation of the claim, determine whether the metes and bounds of the claimed invention are clear and whether there is more than one reasonable interpretation of what is covered by the claim.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See PART 1, sections II-III of the 2011 Supplementary 112 Guidelines and MPEP 2173 et seq. Check for problematic term types: functional terms that merely recite a problem/result rather than structure/material/steps; terms of degree/subjective terms (and whether the specification provides a standard for measuring them); unclear Markush groups (whether a skilled artisan can envision all members); inconsistencies between claim and specification that prevent determining scope. For each §112, ¶6 limitation, determine whether the written description discloses the corresponding structure/material/acts linking to the claimed function—if not, reject under §112, ¶2. If metes and bounds are unclear, reject as indefinite (FP 7.34.01).

rubrics_metrics.name: Proper dependent claim requirements (35 U.S.C. §112, ¶4)
rubrics_metrics.description: Determine whether dependent claims comply with ¶4 by properly specifying further limitations and including all limitations of the claim upon which they depend.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a dependent claim fails to specify a further limitation of the subject matter or fails to include all the limitations of the claim upon which it depends, reject the dependent claim under §112, ¶4 as unpatentable. Ensure claim dependency format and incorporation of limitations are correct.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clearly communicate findings, conclusions, and their bases in an Office action; practice compact prosecution
rubrics_metrics.description: When making a rejection under 35 U.S.C. §112, identify the particular claim language giving rise to the rejection and state the specific reason that the identified language does not comply with the relevant paragraph. Evaluate claims for patentability under all applicable statutes and attempt resolution through interview.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In Office actions include findings under §101, §102, §103, and non-statutory double patenting as applicable; raise any formal objections; and attempt to resolve issues via examiner-applicant interview to promote compact prosecution. For §112 rejections, explicitly cite the claim terms, the deficiency, and the statutory paragraph relied upon.
